Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb57aaf4a2315b02a9a2f05bbb639177125807d2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher-membership-resolved-principal.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/api-endpoint-step.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx, content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx, content/docs/ai/agents.mdx, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.mcp-oauth.test.ts, .changeset/environment-membership-judges-resolved-principal.md (read for ②)

No card, by the maintainer's ruling for this series; `Refs #28284` is the series mailbox, closed, with nothing on it about this PR. Why line, as fixed: 「QA 第三轮发现的安全加固(细节按披露裁决不公开)」.

Check-runs on the head at the time of writing: 47 runs, 42 completed (29 `success`, 13 `skipped`, none failed, none cancelled), 5 still in progress (`Test Core` shards 1 to 5). Among the completed successes: `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` shards 6 to 8, every `Type Check` family, every `Lint` family, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts this record relies on; the verdict below stands on the diff and the completed runs, the seat gates landing on the remaining runs finishing green, and a red run reopens this record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of the dispatcher's scoped routes on a multi-environment host, narrowed on one class of caller.** `HttpDispatcher.enforceProjectMembership` (http-dispatcher.ts 1589-1815 on the head) runs after `resolveRequestScope` and the ADR-0069 gate and before every domain body (`dispatch()` 2942-2962), for every route except the control-plane skip list (`/auth`, `/cloud`, `/health`, `/ready`, `/discovery`), the share-link resolve and messages routes, the exact approvals act route, the inbound hook `POST`, requests with no `environmentId`, and the system environment. On a request a host `KernelResolver` placed in an environment, a caller admitted by an API key (any of those routes) or by an OAuth access token (`/mcp`, plain or environment-scoped spelling, the only face that accepts one) is now judged as the resolved principal — the key's owner or the token's user — and refused `403 PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED` when that user holds no `sys_environment_member` row in the resolved environment. **Right** against the published contract on `main`: `api.enforceProjectMembership` is declared as the "Per-environment membership 403 gate (dispatcher)" (stack.zod.ts 1073), `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx` says every request an environment resolves is served "behind the same project-membership and capability gates as the scoped URL", `dispatch()`'s own preamble says the gate holds scoped data, meta, AI and automation routes on `sys_environment_member`, and nothing on `main` declares a credential-shaped exemption.
2. **The admitting-credential test is read off facts the identity step already writes.** `context.admission.credential === 'api_key'` is written by the shared key-admission seam through `onAdmission` (resolve-execution-context.ts 297; resolve-authz-context.ts 620-626); `principalKind === 'agent'` is decided by the shared assembler on an OAuth client (`assemble-execution-context.ts` 320, 343); `oauthScopes` is set only from an OAuth provenance (396). A session-admitted human carries none of the three. **Right**, with one cohesion finding in ④ (should-fix 1).
3. **The organization the bearer arm hands the platform bypass is the vetted one.** `executionContext.tenantId` for a key is the row's `active_organization_id`, server-written at mint from the minter's active organization (keys.ts 349-358) and refused as `organization_membership_ended` when no current membership backs it under a wall (resolve-authz-context.ts 716-724); for a token it is the consent organization the verifier returns, vetted by `vetOrganizationClaim` on the session arm (resolve-execution-context.ts 258-268; resolve-authz-context.ts 795-812), the same rule `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` publishes. It is the value every `/meta` and `/packages` door already reads through `resolveActiveOrganizationId`. **Right.**
4. **Precedence when two credentials ride one request.** A key beside a cookie, or a token beside a cookie on `/mcp`: the bearer decides, as the identity step already decides it (a key sets the principal before the session arm is reached; a presented token never falls back to a cookie) and as `enforceAuthGate` judges it under ruling C′ item 3. **Right**, and pinned (test case 3).
5. **A failed session read no longer fails open for a bearer-admitted principal.** The `else if (sessionUnread) return null` sits behind the bearer arm, so the gate judges a key or token principal whether or not the cookie read answered; a session-only request keeps the fail-open. **Right**: that read is not the bearer principal's admission.
6. **Unchanged, verified by reading:** single-environment hosts (no resolver, so no `environmentId`: return at 1667), `api.enforceProjectMembership: false` (1594), the skip list and the three token-is-the-authorisation exemptions, the system environment, the session-admitted path (same read, same organization claim, same fail-open), the refusal shape (`403`, `code: PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED`, `details: { environmentId, userId }` as `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx` documents it — the user named is now the one judged), the positive-membership cache keyed `environment:user`. **Right.**
7. **Public surface: unchanged.** No export, type or schema moves; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
8. **Pins.** The new file drives `dispatch()` on a stub multi-environment host with a tenant kernel: refusal and membership-read for a token non-member, for a token non-member beside a member's cookie, and for a key non-member; passage with one read for a token member and a key member; the cookie non-member CONTROL; the no-credential CONTROL (not judged here, as before). The seven cases match the derived judgments above. Red-first and restore readings in the PR body are consistent with the tree; not reproduced (read-only).

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/runtime`: patch.** Right: a bug fix in a released package, no protocol kind, and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.
- **`Clause-②: no` — correctly `no`, not `no (narrowing)`.** The capability the package declares is the per-environment membership 403 gate on scoped routes, in the stack schema, the routing docs and the dispatcher's own preamble; none of them declares that a caller admitted by a key or a token is served a scoped route without being a member, and no published text promises such a caller anything on an environment they are not a member of. What this PR refuses is therefore not a declared capability taken away at the consumer but the spec's own refusal delivered for the remaining credentials — an implementation gap closed where it sits, which is the ⑧ reading the hand-back offers and the one this record confirms. Nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so there is no FROM-to-TO migration to carry. Precedents in this series, #31263 and #31320, declared `Clause-②: no` at `patch` for a refusal newly made real on the same basis and were reviewed and merged on it. The record is nonetheless rendered on the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, so the scrutiny a `no (narrowing)` would owe was applied. Both declaration lines are present and identical in the PR body and the changeset; the changeset body names the package, the level, who is refused, who is not, and the two unchanged host postures.
- **Disclosure check.** PR title and body (both languages), commit message, changeset body, the new source comment, the new test file's header and case names were read. All stay at the level of behaviour: which callers are refused, which are not, where the check sits, what the refusal answers, and the maintainer's fixed why line. The verification paragraph lists which cases are red against `main`'s blob, which is the same level as the body's own 「会被新拒绝的只有」 line and the precedents' verification sections. No sentence states the mechanism the ruling keeps private. No breach.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flag: "Clause-②: no on the ⑧ reading — the reviewer judges."** Answered in ②: `no` stands.
- **Flag: the platform bypass for a bearer principal uses the vetted organization, not a raw claim.** Confirmed in the tree (① 3).
- **Flag: reach is a host with a `kernel-resolver`; none ships in this repository; no end-to-end multi-environment boot measured.** Confirmed by reading (`isMultiTenantHost`, `environment-routing.mdx`: multi-environment hosts ship from a separate distribution). The stub-resolver pins through `dispatch()` are the right instrument here; accepted. The dogfood battery never sets an `environmentId`, so it cannot reach this check; accepted.
- **Flag: the first cut keyed the arm on a disagreement between two reads and was withdrawn.** The withdrawal is right: that rule reached session-admitted principals whose two reads can differ for reasons unrelated to the credential. The credential-keyed arm is the correct discriminator; see ④ should-fix 1 for how it should be spelled.
- **Row ⑩-a (out of scope, not done).** One pre-existing observation outside this PR, not opened or widened by it. **Escalated** as its own private item in this series.
- **Found in review, outside this PR (two items).** Both pre-existing, neither opened or widened by this PR. **Escalated** as their own private items; details stay off GitHub under the disclosure ruling.
- **Hand-back verification claims** (red-first 5 failed / 2 passed against `main`'s blob, restored 7/7, runtime suite 556 files / 8964 tests, tsc 0, eslint 0, 67/67 derived gates): consistent with my reading of the tree; not reproduced; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts.
- No open question in the hand-back is left unanswered.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing was read against the published spec on `main` and the live code, and the gate was pushed on every caller shape that reaches it.

- **Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. The capability declared is the membership gate itself; a key or a token is a way of being admitted as a user, and nothing on `main` promises that user a scoped route in an environment they are not a member of. The refusal routes to the same remedy a cookie non-member has: membership in that environment.
- **Does it make the spec's own refusal real?** Yes. The gate now judges the one principal the request executes as, whichever credential admitted it, which is what the schema line, the routing docs and the dispatcher's preamble already say it does.
- **Shapes tried.** Every credential kind and combination the gate can meet, the bypass, and the failure paths around admission (detail kept off this record under the disclosure ruling). None reaches past the gate after this PR.
- **Should-fix 1** (`http-dispatcher.ts`, the new `bearerAdmitted` predicate): the gate infers "a bearer admitted this principal" from three facts, one of which is the admission channel (`admission.credential`) and two of which are envelope fields (`principalKind`, `oauthScopes`) that the shared assembler derives from the same provenance. The identity step already knows which credential admitted the principal and already reports it on `onAdmission` for a key; a token-admitted principal is reported there as `'session'`, which is why the gate reaches past it. Report the token provenance on the admission channel too (one more value on `RequestAdmission.credential`, written where the established session for a token is built) and have the gate read that one fact. Today the three disjuncts are value-identical to it, so no behaviour changes; the finding is a second spelling of the admission fact, which a future provenance could drift from.
- **Nit** (test file): the key arm is pinned on `/mcp` only, while it holds on every dispatcher route; one scoped data or meta route with a key would pin the route-independence. No effect on correctness or the contract.
- No must-fix.
